title: Restriction of module sheaves to a slice is exact
statement: Let (C,J) be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], R a sheaf of rings, and U an object. Restriction of R-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] to R|U-module sheaves on C/U [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] preserves finite limits and finite colimits.

source.place: Tag 093U, lemma-kernel-finite-locally-constant (3), restriction of module sheaves to a slice is exact

proof.text: For underlying abelian sheaves, restriction along the slice forgetful functor is both a right adjoint and, by cocontinuity, a left adjoint. It therefore preserves finite limits and colimits. These adjunctions exist since the site is small and abelian groups admit the required Kan extensions.

Restriction of modules commutes with taking the underlying abelian sheaf. The underlying-sheaf functor is faithful and preserves finite limits and colimits by the module sheafification construction. It reflects short exactness. Apply the preceding preservation result to the underlying short exact sequence to prove preservation by module restriction.
The additive exact-functor criterion in an abelian category turns preservation of short exact sequences into preservation of finite limits and finite colimits.
